concepts.gloss: Positive or negative syntactic status of a clause, diagnosed by its distribution rather than simply by the presence of a negative word.
A test of a clause's positive or negative status using a permitted continuation, confirmation tag, or prenuclear inversion.
A prosodically detached supplementary continuation whose negative form presupposes a negative host clause.
An interrogative tag that seeks confirmation and bears the opposite polarity from the host clause.
A reduced follow-up clause whose connective reflects the preceding clause's syntactic polarity, such as neither/nor versus so.
A negative-marked constituent before the nucleus whose position triggers obligatory subject–auxiliary inversion.

rules.concept: subject–auxiliary inversion with prenuclear negative constituents
rules.statement: When the negation of a clause is carried by a constituent in the prenucleus, subject–auxiliary inversion is obligatory in the main clause.
rules.condition: In a main clause with a negative constituent such as not once or at no time in prenuclear position, invert the finite auxiliary and subject; insert supportive do if needed. The trigger must be the prenuclear negative constituent, not simply the presence of negation elsewhere in the clause.
rules.violation: A main clause begins with a negative-marked prenuclear constituent but retains uninverted subject–finite auxiliary order.

correct.text: Not once did the council meet.
At no time did the visitors complain.
After the lecture, Mina didn't feel well. [negative marker on the verb, not the prenuclear adjunct]
Only occasionally did Mina attend the lectures. [inversion triggered by only, not by a negative constituent]
